events.title: Isaac Singer Patents His Sewing Machine
events.description: American inventor Isaac Singer was granted a patent for his sewing machine design. It used a practical up-and-down needle and a foot treadle. Both features made home and factory sewing much faster.
events.significance: Singer's machine helped mechanize the clothing industry and became one of the first widely sold household appliances.

events.title: Asaph Hall Discovers Deimos
events.description: American astronomer Asaph Hall discovered Deimos, the smaller of Mars's two moons. He found it at the U.S. Naval Observatory in Washington, D.C.
events.significance: The discovery of Mars's moons deepened understanding of our neighboring planet, and the moons still draw scientific interest today.

events.title: Soviet Union Detonates Its First Hydrogen Bomb
events.description: The Soviet Union tested its first hydrogen bomb, a thermonuclear device far more powerful than earlier atomic weapons. The test took place at the Semipalatinsk site in Kazakhstan.
events.significance: The test intensified the Cold War arms race and showed that both superpowers now held thermonuclear weapons.

events.title: The IBM Personal Computer Goes on Sale
events.description: The IBM PC, also known as the IBM 5150, reached stores for the first time. It had no disk drives as standard and sold for about $1,500.
events.significance: IBM's entry into the market helped set the standard for personal computers and brought them into offices and homes worldwide.

events.title: Sue the T. rex Is Discovered
events.description: Fossil hunter Sue Hendrickson found the remains of a Tyrannosaurus rex in South Dakota. The skeleton, nicknamed Sue, is one of the largest and most complete ever found.
events.significance: Sue became a landmark find in paleontology and a star attraction at Chicago's Field Museum.
